title: Playground Turf in Mead, CO: Daycares and Parks | NoCo Turf Co.
description: In Mead's residential zones a small child care center needs a conditional use permit; a home daycare doesn't. Six town parks had playgrounds in 2025.
h1: In every Mead residential district, a small child care center needs a conditional use permit and a home daycare does not.
lede: That split decides whether a play yard with turf can open on a Mead street without a separate permit review. Under the equipment, the state license sets the surface, and at the Town's own playgrounds residents have asked for something other than wood chips.

answer.question: Can a Mead home daycare put turf under its play equipment?
answer.answer: Zoning isn't the obstacle: a family child care home is allowed by right in all five Mead residential districts, and Colorado's licensing rules accept artificial turf with a built-in resilient pad under climbing equipment. NoCo Turf Co. installs playground turf in Mead, Colorado.

blocks.h2: Mead's use table sends small child care centers to a conditional use permit in RSF-E, RSF-1, RSF-4, RMF-8 and RMF-14.
blocks.takeaway: A large center is allowed by right only in the HC and GC districts, and is a conditional use in RMF-14, DMU and LI.
paras: The land use code defines a small center as one licensed by the state for fewer than 15 children and a large center as one licensed for 16 or more, which leaves a 15-child center without a category. It depends on the license, so ask Mead Planning which row applies.

A family child care home is marked allowed in all five residential districts, and Mead exempts it from the 10-client-a-day cap on home occupations, leaving capacity to state rules. That part is not a Mead choice. Not legal advice: since HB21-1222, Colorado has required every local government to treat a family child care home as a residential use in its zoning, fire, sanitation and building rules.

blocks.h2: Colorado's family child care rules count artificial turf with a built-in pad as an approved surface.
paras: Not legal advice. Under the state's family child care home rules, climbing and sliding equipment, or equipment with attached platforms, 18 inches or higher needs at least 6 inches of resilient surfacing in its use zone, and newly installed solid surfacing needs the manufacturer's written statement that it meets current federal requirements. The [safety guides](/guides/safety/) cover how a turf pad is rated for fall height.

blocks.h2: Six of Mead's nine town park sites had playgrounds in 2025, and the oldest are due for new ones.
paras: The Town's park list, archived in April 2025, shows playground equipment at Feather Ridge Estates Park, Founders Park, Liberty Ranch Park, Margil Farms Park, Mead Town Park and North Creek Park. By August 2025 the Town had replaced the Margil Farms playground and was finishing North Creek's, and its park report expected the oldest parks to need new playgrounds within about five years.

Residents have views on what goes underneath. Early feedback for the park plan asked for updated playgrounds at Town Park, Ames Park and Founders Park, and one questionnaire answer asked for ground cover other than wood chips, after too many shoes full of wood and splinters.

blocks.h2: Where new Mead homes are far from a park, the developer builds a pocket park with live ground cover.
paras: Section 16-2-120 requires a one-acre pocket park for homes more than a quarter mile from a neighborhood or community park, with live ground cover, trees and irrigation plus one feature such as playground equipment. Neighborhood parks run 7 acres or more and can include playground equipment too.

About half of Mead's public parks are owned and maintained by an HOA or metro district rather than the Town. The code doesn't say whether turf under a new pocket-park playground counts toward that live ground cover. It depends on the approved plan, so ask Mead Planning before specifying it.

faq.q: Are Mead's school playgrounds and fields open to the public?
faq.a: Not through the Town any more. St. Vrain Valley runs an elementary, middle and high school in Mead, but the Town's joint-use agreement for district recreation facilities has expired, so they are no longer available for public use under it.

faq.q: How far does the padding have to reach around a home daycare's climber?
faq.a: Not legal advice. Colorado's family child care rules set a 6-foot use zone around preschool and school-age climbing and sliding equipment, 3 feet around toddler equipment and 6 feet out from the base of a toddler slide. Toddler climbers top out at 32 inches.

faq.q: Does a backyard playset on turf need a Mead permit?
faq.a: Mead's online code, current to Ord. No. 1075 of April 2025, has no artificial-turf section, and a single-family building permit needs no landscape plan. A playset that counts as an accessory structure has to meet its district's setbacks and stay off any recorded easement, so check the plat and ask Mead Planning.
